detailed_description: The SQL Generator creates a simple SQL snippet from visible browser-side form fields. You can choose SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or CREATE TABLE, edit the table name and relevant fields, and copy the generated text. SELECT includes columns, WHERE, ORDER BY, and LIMIT fields. INSERT uses columns and values. UPDATE uses a SET clause and WHERE clause. DELETE uses a WHERE clause. CREATE TABLE uses a freeform schema definition textarea. The tool does not choose SQL dialects, validate schema references, upload database schemas, build JOINs or subqueries, analyze execution plans, provide syntax highlighting, export files, create transaction wrappers, or guarantee production-ready SQL.
usage_steps: Choose SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or CREATE TABLE.
Enter the table name and edit the fields shown for that command.
For SELECT, edit columns, WHERE, ORDER BY, and LIMIT values.
For CREATE TABLE, edit the schema definition textarea.
Review the generated SQL text and copy it when it is useful as a starting point.
usage_examples: Draft a simple SELECT query for one table while prototyping.
Create a basic INSERT statement from pasted column and value lists.
Generate an UPDATE or DELETE statement with a manually written WHERE clause.
Sketch a starter CREATE TABLE statement before reviewing it in your database tool.
